scope: One fresh local Kind v0.32.0 cluster with exactly two Kubernetes nodes (one control-plane node and one worker), Kubernetes v1.36.1, and pinned Cilium 1.20.5 in IPv4 native routing mode. Two case-owned BusyBox endpoints run on different nodes. The case sends only their fixed synthetic HTTP markers over IPv4 TCP/18080. Red runs with Cilium encryption disabled. Green enables Cilium WireGuard, checks Cilium status, both configured peer address sets and live interface counters, and repeats the marker request. Positive verifies the reverse marker path. This tests Cilium-managed cross-node pod-to-pod traffic only. It does not test same-node traffic, host-to-host/node-to-pod paths, other CNIs, every cluster route/interface, production coverage, performance, or packet contents. No packet capture, public destination, real credential, or external network is used.

checks.claim: Encryption is disabled and the exact cross-node marker remains readable
Cilium configures reciprocal WireGuard coverage for both fixture endpoints
The WireGuard interface receives the cross-node response traffic
The reverse cross-node path works through the configured WireGuard interface
